newsitem.title: USA: CBOT SOYOIL ENDS UP ON EXPORTS, MEAL MIXED.
newsitem.headline: CBOT SOYOIL ENDS UP ON EXPORTS, MEAL MIXED.

text.p: CBOT soyoil futures ended higher Tuesday on rumors of Chinese interest in U.S. soyoil and a U.S. Department of Agriculture forecast indicating an increase in U.S. soyoil exports, traders and analysts said.
Soymeal ended mixed, with most contracts lower on soyoil/soymeal spreading, traders said.
Because U.S. soyoil values are now competitive with those in South America, soyoil traders said China was actively seeking soyoil for September and October shipment.
U.S. exporters could not confirm a sale, but several said China was seeking freight for the shipment of one cargo.
Soyoil futures also received support from USDA's latest supply and demand report. The forecast released Tuesday pegged soyoil exports for 1997/98 at 2.150 billion lbs, up from 2.050 a month ago.
"I think we easily could rebound (soy)oil demand to that level in 1997/98," said Mark Widener, oilseed analyst with Cargill Investor Services.

December soyoil ended 0.51 cent per lb higher at 22.62 cents, and other months were up 0.47 to 0.54. December soymeal ended down $1.90 per ton at $199.30, with other months up $0.60 a ton to down $3.50.
Widener said U.S. soyoil exports would pick up this fall because inventories of importing nations were running low and purchases would soon be needed to replenish them.
On the day, ADM bought 800 lots of September soymeal and Griffin Trading sold 300 lots January and 400 lots December, pit sources said.
In soyoil trade, Produce Grain bought 500 lots December and Tenco bought 300 lots December. ADM sold 500 December and Cargill sold 400 September and 100 December, traders said.
Soymeal futures volume was estimated by CBOT at 20,000 lots, against Monday's 13,929. Soyoil volume was pegged at 17,000 lots against Monday's 13,427.
